catalyst_text: Reported positive Phase 2 results met primary endpoints
detailed_catalyst_text: A 16-week readout from the randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 2 APEX Part B study in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis showed the trial met its primary and key secondary endpoints. Mid-dose achieved EASI-75 in 65.9% versus 23.4% on placebo, with a safety profile consistent with other agents in class, indicating robust efficacy.
catalyst_text_evidence: Apogee Therapeutics, Inc. ... today announced positive 16-week data from Part B of the Phase 2 APEX clinical trial of zumilokibart (APG777) ... in patients with moderate-to-severe AD. The trial met its primary and secondary endpoints with high statistical significance including 65.9% of patients treated with mid-dose zumilokibart achieving EASI-75 (41.9% placebo adjusted). Zumilokibart was well tolerated, with a safety profile generally consistent with other agents in the class.

catalyst_text: Announced positive 52 week Phase 2 maintenance results
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported 52-week maintenance results from Part A of a Phase 2 study in moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, showing durable responses with both every-3-month and every-6-month dosing. High rates of EASI-75 and vIGA 0/1 maintenance and deepening of lesional and itch responses were observed, with safety generally consistent with class. These data support a differentiated profile with less frequent dosing.
catalyst_text_evidence: Apogee Therapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:APGE) ... today announced positive 52-week maintenance data from Part A of the Phase 2 APEX clinical trial of zumilokibart (APG777), a potential best-in-class anti-IL-13 antibody, in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (AD). The results demonstrated durable maintenance of response with both 3- and 6- month maintenance dosing regimens. Maintenance of Eczema Area and Severity Index percent score reductions of at least 75 (EASI-75) among Week 16 responder population by 75% and 85% of patients with every 3-month and 6-month dosing, respectively. Validated Investigator's Global Assessment (vIGA) 0/1 maintenance of response of 86% for 3-month dosing and 78% for 6-month dosing among Week 16 responder population. Well tolerated across the full 52-week study with a safety profile generally consistent with other agents in the class.

catalyst_text: Announced positive interim Phase 1b results in asthma
detailed_catalyst_text: The company reported positive interim results from a double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1b trial in adults with mild-to-moderate asthma and elevated FeNO. A single 720 mg dose showed a favorable safety profile and robust, durable FeNO suppression through 16 weeks, with some patients maintaining suppression to 32 weeks. These results support potential infrequent dosing and further development in asthma.
catalyst_text_evidence: "Today, the company announced positive interim data from its Phase 1b double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating the safety and tolerability of zumilokibart in 19 adult patients with mild-to-moderate asthma and a fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) baseline greater or equal to 25 parts per billion (ppb) which represents an enriched Type 2 inflammation population." "In the trial, zumilokibart demonstrated: Favorable safety profile; zumilokibart was well-tolerated in patients with mild-to-moderate asthma." "Maximum absolute mean FeNO reduction of 45 ppb (60% decrease from baseline) after single dose. Durable FeNO suppression through 16 weeks for all patients. Suppression of FeNO through 32 weeks for patients with available follow up, supporting potential for 3- or 6-month dosing."
